accepted.reason: "textColour" (role "text") is a parent-level styling attr on sgs/accordion-item, which also mounts a sgs/text InnerBlock for that same role. sgs/text owns real typography/colour controls for itself — whichever wins on CSS specificity, the client is shown two places to set the same visual property. Verify: does the parent attr actually still drive rendered CSS, or is it a dead-by-specificity leftover (check-dead-controls' angle) that should be removed in favour of the child's own controls?

sources: sgs/text (mounted via this block's InnerBlocks template, role "text"): its own native typography/colour controls
accepted.reason: ACCEPTED 2026-08-20 (shop-archive Wave 2, P1-6). Introduced deliberately: sgs/hero's root previously mapped css:background-color to native:color.background while declaring no supports.color at all, so the mapping pointed at an attribute WordPress never registers and the block's existing textColourHover was bound to nothing. Adding root backgroundColour/textColour repairs that. This finding is the SAME CLASS already accepted for sgs/accordion-item (identical attr, identical keeper) - consistent treatment, not new slack. Substantively the two controls are not the same control: hero's root textColour sets an INHERITED cascade default for every text descendant (including non-sgs/text children), whereas the child sgs/text control overrides one instance. The duplication the gate objects to is real as a UX question - two places in the inspector reading as 'text colour'. HANDED TO the colour-golden track: it owns colour standardisation and should rule on this pattern once, across every parent that mounts sgs/text, rather than per block. See .claude/reports/2026-08-20-HANDOVER-3-shop-wave-2-to-colour-golden-track.md item 2.

sources: sgs/text (mounted via this block's InnerBlocks template, role "text"): its own native typography/colour controls
accepted.reason: ACCEPTED 2026-08-21. Surfaced by the American-to-British rename of this block's own textColor -> textColour, which is what made the gate recognise it as a colour attr; the control itself is unchanged and predates the rename. Same class already accepted for sgs/accordion-item and sgs/hero: a parent-level textColour on a block that also mounts sgs/text children. Substantively the two are not the same control - the parent sets an INHERITED cascade default for every text descendant, the child overrides one instance - but the UX objection is real, and the pattern should be ruled on once across every parent that mounts sgs/text rather than per block.

sources: sgs/text (mounted via this block's InnerBlocks template, role "text"): its own native typography/colour controls
accepted.reason: ACCEPTED 2026-08-21. Introduced by retiring this block from WordPress's native colour path: it previously had supports.color.text true, so the same duplication existed via the NATIVE control and was invisible to this gate. Making the colour SGS-owned did not create the overlap, it made it visible. Same class as sgs/accordion-item, sgs/hero and sgs/cta-section; belongs to the single cross-block ruling on parents that mount sgs/text.
